sections.heading: C — Night, winter, slippery roads, skids and hydroplaning
sections.markdown:
## C — Night, winter, slippery roads, skids and hydroplaning

FACT_ID: sec11-F01 | anchor: A71
Most drivers learn under normal conditions, so safe driving in changing weather, light or emergencies must be learned through study and experience. [A71]
Source: [A71 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec11-F02 | anchor: A71
About half of Alabama's fatal crashes happen during darkness, even though traffic is light then. [A71]
Source: [A71 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec11-F03 | anchor: A71
Never overdrive your headlights: keep a speed at which you can stop within the distance your lights show ahead. [A71]
Source: [A71 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec11-F04 | anchor: A71
Under normal conditions, high beams usually light the road about 350 feet ahead. [A71]
Source: [A71 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec11-F05 | anchor: A71
The law requires dimming your headlights within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle and within 200 feet of a vehicle you are following. [A71]
Why it matters: the oncoming distance is the longer one; the following distance is shorter.
Source: [A71 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec11-F06 | anchor: A71
If an oncoming driver keeps high beams on after you dim, keep yours dimmed anyway, since blinding that driver only endangers you. [A71]
Source: [A71 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec11-F07 | anchor: A71
Keep lights working and lenses clean, and keep all vehicle glass clean, free of defects and clear of frost and steam. [A71]
Source: [A71 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec11-F08 | anchor: A71
State law requires headlights, not just parking lights, starting a half-hour after sunset and lasting until a half-hour before sunrise, and also whenever you cannot see clearly for at least 500 feet. [A71]
Source: [A71 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec11-F09 | anchor: A71
When unsure whether lights are needed, turn them on low beam, which helps you see and helps others see you. [A71]
Source: [A71 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec11-F10 | anchor: A71
At night watch closely for signs, pedestrians, bicycles, slow vehicles and animals, and study maps ahead of time. [A71]
Source: [A71 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec11-F11 | anchor: A72
A companion can act as a second pair of eyes for signs and hazards, and moving your eyes from near to far and side to side eases night eye fatigue. [A72]
Source: [A72 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec11-F12 | anchor: A72
To cut glare from oncoming lights, look away toward the right edge of the pavement and its white line. [A72]
Source: [A72 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec11-F13 | anchor: A72
For glare from behind, use a day-night mirror or adjust the mirror to block most of the light. [A72]
Source: [A72 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec11-F14 | anchor: A72
In a night breakdown, pull well off the road, turn on four-way flashers, raise the hood, and stay with the car if you can. [A72]
Source: [A72 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec11-F15 | anchor: A72
If you must walk, carry a light and walk on the left edge facing traffic, and place flares or reflectors 100 to 500 feet behind the car on the right edge. [A72]
Source: [A72 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec11-F16 | anchor: A72
Speed is more dangerous at night because at high speed your headlight range does not give enough stopping distance, so obey limits even on roads you know. [A72]
Source: [A72 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec11-F17 | anchor: A72
Winter adds darkness, fog, rain, snow, sleet and ice, and in most cases bad weather alone cannot be blamed for crashes. [A72]
Source: [A72 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec11-F18 | anchor: A72
Warm the engine while clearing snow and ice from the car and windows, and keep washer fluid mixed with anti-freeze. [A72]
Source: [A72 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec11-F19 | anchor: A72
In extreme cold, avoid using washers at high speed, since the fluid can freeze on the glass and block your view. [A72]
Source: [A72 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec11-F20 | anchor: A72
Test your brakes gently at low speed to learn how slippery the road is, then set your speed to match. [A72]
Source: [A72 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec11-F21 | anchor: A73
Snow treads on the drive wheels improve traction in snow, but you still drive below normal speed and leave more stopping room. [A73]
Source: [A73 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec11-F22 | anchor: A73
Snow treads do not grip ice; for severe ice, hard-packed snow or very deep snow, reinforced tire chains are best. [A73]
Source: [A73 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec11-F23 | anchor: A73
Alabama law requires headlights whenever wipers are running for rain, sleet or snow, but intermittent wiper use does not require them. [A73]
Source: [A73 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec11-F24 | anchor: A73
On snow or ice a car needs three to twelve times the stopping distance it needs on dry pavement, so keep well back. [A73]
Source: [A73 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec11-F25 | anchor: A73
To start on snow or ice, keep engine speed very low; with a clutch release it slowly or use second or high gear, and with an automatic accelerate gently. [A73]
Source: [A73 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec11-F26 | anchor: A73
On packed snow or ice brake gently, and for a sudden stop pump the brakes, easing off whenever the wheels lock or start to slip, without pushing in the clutch. [A73]
Source: [A73 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec11-F27 | anchor: A73
A skid happens when the tires lose their grip, and then the engine, brakes and even steering lose effect. [A73]
Source: [A73 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec11-F28 | anchor: A73
Do not brake in a skid until you regain your forward direction, since braking speeds the skid and locked front wheels lose steering. [A73]
Why it matters: slamming the brakes is the instinct the manual warns against.
Source: [A73 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec11-F29 | anchor: A73
To end a skid, keep the rear from outrunning the front; in a rear-wheel drive car, easing off the gas slows the rear wheels and, with steering, straightens the car. [A73]
Source: [A73 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec11-F30 | anchor: A74
In a front-wheel drive car, a light touch on the gas speeds the front wheels so the front catches up and the skid straightens. [A74]
Why it matters: front-wheel and rear-wheel drive skids call for opposite pedal actions.
Source: [A74 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec11-F31 | anchor: A74
Without room to accelerate, the next best step is to disengage the transmission and steer the way the rear is skidding, though many experts warn against shifting to neutral in a panic. [A74]
Source: [A74 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec11-F32 | anchor: A74
On wet roads most tires wipe the surface up to 35 mph, but in a standard car partial hydroplaning starts near 35 mph and can become total near 55 mph. [A74]
Source: [A74 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec11-F33 | anchor: A74
With total hydroplaning there is no friction to brake, speed up or turn, so wind or a slight curve can cause an uncontrollable skid. [A74]
Source: [A74 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec11-F34 | anchor: A74
If you hydroplane, take your foot off the accelerator; correct a partial-hydroplane skid, but in a total one just release the gas and ride it out. [A74]
Source: [A74 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec11-F35 | anchor: A74
Good tires with deep tread help prevent hydroplaning, but when water is deeper than the tread, expect complete hydroplaning above 50 mph. [A74]
Source: [A74 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0074]

Glossary: overdriving headlights — driving too fast to stop within your lighted distance [A71]. Skid — the tires losing their grip on the road [A73]. Hydroplaning — tires riding on a film of water instead of the road [A74].
Memory aid: rear-wheel drive skid, ease off the gas; front-wheel drive skid, a little gas [A74].
